section_1.title: Introduction: The Heartbeat of Music
section_1.content: Define 'Measure' as a vessel for time. Introduce the pulse (beat) and the concept of time signatures as fractional constraints on musical flow.
section_1.example: Visualize a robotic drummer 'Tic-Toc' hitting a drum at a steady, constant interval, defining the basic 'pulse'.

section_2.title: The Anatomy of a Measure (Time Signatures)
section_2.content: Explain the time signature fraction. The top number represents 'beats per measure' (numerator), and the bottom number represents the 'note value' that gets one beat (denominator).
section_2.example: Show a 4/4 time signature. A visual animation of a 'pizza pie' cut into 4 slices; each measure must hold exactly one whole pie's worth of notes.

section_3.title: Mathematical Division of Time
section_3.content: Prerequisite: Basic fractions. Connect note lengths (Whole, Half, Quarter, Eighth) to powers of 2 (1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Show how they sum up to equal the measure capacity.
section_3.example: Animated 'Tetris' blocks falling into a measure box: two quarter notes (1/4 + 1/4) plus one half note (1/2) perfectly filling the 4/4 container.

section_4.title: Complex Meters and Syncopation
section_4.content: Introduce compound meters (e.g., 6/8) to show how division isn't always linear. Explain that math in music allows for 'stress' (accents) on specific beats.
section_4.example: A group of squirrels gathering nuts: they dance in groups of three (1-2-3, 1-2-3), illustrating the 'swing' or 'triplet' feel compared to the standard binary count.

section_5.title: Application: The Composer’s Equation
section_5.content: Summarize how measure theory acts as the 'grammar' for music, allowing different instruments to synchronize perfectly through shared numerical structures.
section_5.example: Display a split-screen: A pianist and a violinist playing different melodies, but their 'measure bars' align perfectly like synchronized gears in a clock.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=24, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.8).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)
